stability: MCP tool names and input schemas are additive: existing names never change meaning, and new capability arrives as new tools. Repository routes are named by method and path; a route that moves or is removed breaks every agent written against this contract.

tools.name: okf.validate
tools.summary: Validate an OKF document and return the validation report

tools.name: graph.stats
tools.summary: Graph health of an OKF document: nodes, edges, isolated nodes, components

tools.name: gate.run
tools.summary: Run the round-trip fidelity gate and return its evidence record

tools.name: okf.diff
tools.summary: Semantic diff between two OKF documents: elements, edges and attributes

repositoryHttpSurface.auth: Every endpoint except /health and /version requires the same authentication a human meets and enforces the listed permission plus project scope: an unauthenticated caller is refused 401, an under-privileged caller 403. There is no agent-only path.

endpoints.summary: Liveness; reports the auth mode and never a secret
List projects, filtered to the caller's scope
Commit an OKF document to a branch
Fetch the OKF document behind a commit
Revert a branch to an earlier commit as a new commit
Run the round-trip fidelity gate and record the run
Import a source artifact through a binding; gated and measured
Read an import's loss report and fidelity measurement
Three-way merge one branch into another

agentContract.agentIsAClient: An agent may read and propose; it may not write. An agent token cannot hold a write or admin role, and every write route refuses an agent with 403. There is no privileged agent path and no automated acceptance path yet; a human performs changes through the ordinary routes.
agentContract.documentLevel: The MCP tools above operate on documents supplied in the request and never touch a repository. Repository operations are the HTTP surface.
agentContract.audit: Every write is recorded in the audit log with the actor (the verified subject), the mechanism (open, static, jwt or agent) and, for agents, the authorizer the agent acted for. An agent cannot write today, so no agent entry is recorded yet.
